name: Kakita Kensaku
concept: Kensaku's eyes move to a blade before they move to the person holding it, even when the person is speaking to him.

answers.giri: Kensaku is Kakita Namika's man, lent to the Castle of the Swift Sword; he reports to Matsu Ryōzō, Master of the Forges, and is counted among the War College's staff; he must certify which blades in the Lion armory are sound enough for the field, knowing that a flawed edge he misses could kill the warrior who carries it.
answers.ninjo: Kensaku wants to forge the blade Akodo Tsanuri carries into the field. Tsanuri carries his family's blade, and will die holding it before he sets it down for a Kakita's.
answers.standout_quality: Kensaku has learned to read a workshop's temperament by how the smiths treat their tools and each other, a skill that makes him useful during his visits to repair blades but leaves him uncertain whether he belongs to any forge at all.
answers.accomplishment: He trained the Master of the Forges' hunting hawks to accept handling only from him, so that when the old man's hands began to fail, Kensaku could work the birds without being asked or refused.
answers.challenge: When Kensaku certifies a blade at the Castle of the Swift Sword, he is always aware that he is judging not just the steel but the smith's honor, and he cannot bring himself to do only the first.
answers.peace: At festival grounds where the noise of a crowd breaks into separate voices and paths, Kensaku can move through without needing to know who forged anything, and he does.
answers.fear: When Kensaku must tell a master smith that their work has failed inspection, he finds himself praising the steel instead, and leaves the Castle uncertain whether he has done his duty or protected a reputation at the cost of a Lion warrior's life.
answers.accoutrement: Hawking glove. Matsu Ryōzō's; never given back.

clan_relationship.text: Kensaku's reluctance to trust a blade's maker's name—to set aside his skill and simply certify what he holds—reads to other smiths at the Castle as Crane fastidiousness, which the Lion forgive because his repairs hold, but which keeps him outside their forge's hierarchy in ways he has not resolved.

mentor.name: Ide Tokimochi
mentor.text: Ide Tokimochi taught Kensaku that a blade's pedigree matters more than its quality, and now Kensaku cannot inspect steel without asking whose hands made it—a doubt that keeps him useful to the Lion but useless to himself.

answers.first_impression: Kensaku's eyes move to a blade before they move to the person holding it, even when the person is speaking to him.
answers.stress_reaction: When a blade fails inspection at the Castle, Kensaku begins asking the smith questions about their other work, their training, their family's forges—circling outward until he has filled the silence where the word "failed" should be.
answers.relationships:
Daidoji Rina (Crane) — Daidoji Rina sends word when she travels to the Castle of the Swift Sword, and Kensaku meets her away from the forges to avoid the appearance that a Crane courtier influences his certifications, a caution that has made their conversations shorter and less frequent than either would prefer.
Kakita Shirai (Crane) — Kakita Shirai watches Kensaku work and does not ask him which smiths he trusts, though she could read the answer in his face before he speaks it.
Mirumoto Hisa (Dragon) — Hisa has never asked Kensaku for the duel her students say she wants, and he has never offered it; they have spent two winters instead arguing whether a blade forged for one hand can be trusted in two.
